title: Job block
description: Schema for each entry in the fenced YAML block of plan.md. Written by the CALLER — nothing here decomposes work — and read by the orchestrator (for wave scheduling and scope accounting) and by the agent that runs the job (as its whole assignment).

id.description: Names the job, its branch and its worktree, and the report file it must write. Lowercase, digits and hyphens; unique within the task. `st-2-clip` is the convention for numbered pipeline stages and is not required -- the pattern used to demand `st-<number>-`, which fitted work shaped like this repository's own first task and nothing else. Five named review passes over one diff have no numbers to give.

goal.description: The whole brief. The agent that runs this job gets no plan and no context beyond what is in this block, so a goal it cannot act on alone is a job that will come back wrong.

file_scope.description: Write scope: globs this job may modify. MEASURED, not enforced — files touched outside it are recorded and reported back, never reverted. It is also what buys parallelism: two jobs with overlapping scopes are serialized, and an unscoped job claims everything.

reads.description: Files this subtask depends on but must not modify.

depends_on.description: Job ids that must complete first. Ordering only — parallel safety comes from file_scope. Empty means it can start immediately.

hotspots.description: Unmergeable or high-coupling files this job must touch (engine scenes, project settings, central modules). Taken as exclusive locks, so no two jobs holding one ever run in the same wave.

frozen_interfaces.description: Exact signatures or signals this job must expose for other jobs to code against. Carried into its prompt as a contract it may not change quietly.

estimated_loc.description: Rough changed-line estimate. Recorded so a run shows what was asked for; nothing is computed from it and nothing enforces it.

acceptance.description: What this job has to satisfy, in the caller's own words. Carried into its prompt verbatim. It used to require this protocol's `AC-<n>` ids, which only meant something while an intake stage minted them here.

required_checks.description: Shell commands that are this job's own pass/fail, run by the runtime in this job's worktree after every attempt, immediately after the project-wide `fast` checks from .adg.yaml. All must exit 0 or the attempt counts as failed, and the failure is recorded against THIS job rather than the batch. For what only this job can assert: a project-wide check runs against a tree where the other jobs are still stubs, so it is often limited to compiling. The commands are never shown to the agent -- naming a check command in a prompt costs a turn spent reading it -- so a job that should also self-check before finishing must say so in its `goal`. Omit for the previous behaviour.

tier.description: Which capability band should run this job. t1 cheap and fast, t2 the workhorse, t3 the strongest enrolled. The registry maps each band to a model and a default provider. Advisory: a band nothing enrolled can serve is logged and demoted rather than parking the run.
